en: The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, is a specific species of jasmine known scientifically as Jasminum sambac.
The Philippine carabao, the national animal, is a domesticated swamp buffalo adapted to the country's hot, humid climate.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using simple hand tools.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government is a bicameral Congress composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-step forward, one-step backward dance mimicking a river's current.
Before the Spanish arrived, many Filipinos communicated using Baybayin, an ancient writing system where characters represent syllables rather than single letters.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way television telephone and discovered the physical law of electrical kinetic resistance.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the balcony of his Kawit home.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally demonstrated when neighbors physically carry a nipa hut to a new location.
Filipino citizens acquire the right and duty to vote in national elections once they reach the legal age of eighteen.
